(CE M).GloballyHyperbolic only; the Cauchy surface is derived (exists_cauchy_subset_W0).

hypotheses.note: lem_tube carries the CBG inputs hLine (O2), hSC (O4) of E0CBG.e0Geometry; lem_tube_e0 discharges them by the strict E0LM.e0_globalBTZ and E0LM.e0_secondCountable_of_cauchy (as Surgery.lean does): no added hypothesis.

CylChartData.convex (chart cylinder causally convex in M), proved in exists_cylChartData from strong causality; used by the overlap's causal convexity (mem_U01_of_le), the agreement of the relations (le_iff_U01), the acausality of κ⁻¹Π and exists_overlap_of_le.

hypotheses.paper: 'M0 → M2 is a Cauchy-embedding' (needs M2 GH and Σ Cauchy in M2)
hypotheses.note: CylChartData.globallyHyperbolic_glued and CylChartData.isCauchySurface_glued (the latter now takes [SecondCountableTopology M], carried by its only caller exists_spearDevelopment).

findings: B21 Lemma 2.3's proof (BTZ_1.tex:663) asserts that the gluing M2 is a E_{>=0}-manifold without proving it Hausdorff; it is, for the normalisation chosen here (CylChartData.t2Space_glued: the graph of κ⁻¹ on the overlap is closed because the overlap lies in the compact {v−ε/2 ≤ τ ≤ v+ε/2, r ≤ ε/4} inside the chart cylinder — points of 𝒫 ∩ cyl above Π are in J⁺(κ⁻¹Π), CylChartData.mem_glueF). For a careless choice of the glued piece (e.g. the full closed spear S, as printed, or a piece leaving the chart domain below Π) Hausdorffness can fail; B21 should say which neighbourhood of S is glued. l.672–673 uses CBG universality where it says 'Cauchy-maximal' (IsE0CauchyMaximal.exists_morphism_of_dev).

B21 Lemma 2.3's proof does not argue that M2 is globally hyperbolic: it proves Σ Cauchy in M2 and concludes 'M0 → M2 is a Cauchy-embedding', which in B21's own Def (Cauchy embedding between globally hyperbolic spacetimes) needs GH of M2 first, or a 'Cauchy surface ⇒ GH' theorem for E_{>=0}-manifolds that the paper uses tacitly.

B21 Lemma 2.3's proof (l.642) uses 'a time function whose level sets are C¹ submanifolds' (Bernard–Surh); only a Cauchy surface strictly below the disc Π is needed (CylChartData.exists_cauchy_subset_W0 uses a level of a continuous Cauchy time function, any level below min T on κ⁻¹Π), as SCOPE K-2 noted. B21 also leaves M0's connectedness implicit.

B21 Def 2.1 (l.611–615): with φ(p) = (−2R,0,0) and f = τ − r/2, the head is {f = −2R, r ≤ R} = {r = 2(τ + 2R)}, meeting r = R at τ = −3R/2, and the shaft is {r = R, τ ≥ −3R/2}; the printed {r = 2(τ − R)} and {τ ≥ 0} fit neither this vertex nor each other (the normalisation of Lemma 2.4's proof, Φ(p) = (−R/2,0,0), makes the shaft start at τ = 0). Proved in the corrected form: frontier_spear. U = φ⁻¹(V) is closed, not open; 'neighbourhood of ]p,+∞[' holds (IsSpearNbhd.exists_ray_mem_nhds).

B21 Lemma 2.3's proof (BTZ_1.tex:647) shrinks the chart neighbourhood so that Π is acausal in M, and l.666 ('the boundary of M₀ in M₂ is Π') needs it: without it a causal curve leaving the cylinder from κ⁻¹Π and returning below Π removes points from M₀ that stay as extra points of the spear piece. Formalized: the normalisation holds in the stronger form 'chart cylinder causally convex in M' (CylChartData.convex, proved from strong causality in exists_cylChartData), which gives acausality of κ⁻¹Π (isAcausal_K) and the overlap 𝒫 ∩ cyl ∩ {τ < v+ε/2} (mem_U10_iff). The paper's argument is correct here; round 1's formalization had omitted the normalisation (audit round 2 major), now repaired.

B21 Lemma 2.3's proof (BTZ_1.tex:646–674) needs M₀ = M ∖ J⁺(φ⁻¹Π) connected (CBG developments are connected) and leaves it implicit; it is true for every connected GH E₀-manifold, through the connectedness of a (non-compact) closed Cauchy surface (WP-43a: isConnected_of_isCauchySurface_closed, with R1 = sfa_isCompact_Jplus_inter_Jminus replacing compactness).

DEC-108, B21 Lemma 2.3 (BTZ_1.tex:663–674): the global hyperbolicity of M2 = M0 ∪ 𝒫, never argued in B21, is TRUE and proved directly: M2 is a Causal.Causality.TwoPiece (absolutely minimal charted causality, overlap 𝒫 ∩ {τ < v+ε/2} causally convex in both pieces, relations agreeing) so it is causal and its unmixed diamonds are diamonds of a GH piece; the mixed diamonds J(x,y), x ∈ M0, y ∈ 𝒫 above Π, where M0 and 𝒫 have no common Cauchy surface (so TwoPiece.isCompact_diamond_mixed does not apply), are j(D0) ∪ Ψ(D1) with D1 = {τ ≥ v+ε/2} ∩ J⁻(y) ∩ J⁺(G) compact in 𝔼₀, D0 = J⁺_M(x) ∩ J⁻_M(κ⁻¹H) compact in M (H the points of the disc level below y, G those above x), j the continuous map M0 ∪ κ⁻¹(𝒫 ∩ cyl) → M2 (CylChartData.isCompact_diamond_mixed). The converse inclusion needs that a relation of M from M0 to a point κ⁻¹w of κ⁻¹Π passes through the overlap (exists_overlap_of_le, a connectedness argument on a causal curve), which B21 does not state.

B21 Lemma 2.3's c = c0 ∪ c1 argument (l.668–672): the step 'c1 reaches Π' is the fact that no inextensible causal curve of M2 stays in 𝒫 above Π; proved (CylChartData.not_inextensible_above): read in paper coordinates its past end has τ, r monotone and bounded (τ ≥ v+ε/2), converges in 𝔼₀ (E0.exists_tendsto_of_bddBelow) to a point still in 𝒫, and is adjoined there (pastExtensible_gluePaper). Uniqueness of the intersection needs the causality of M2 (TwoPiece.isCausal) and the acausality of Σ in M; both supplied.
questions: Restricting B21's E_{>=0}-manifolds to E0-manifolds in Lemmas 2.3/2.4 (gx §4 uses E0 only; DEC-77(c) reads maximality among E0-manifolds): accept, which would close lem:tube and the ray row up to Def 2.1's corrected spear?
The vertex coordinate v of a spear chart is left free (the paper's (−2R,0,0) is a τ-translation normalisation, inconsistent with its own head formula). Accept the free-vertex reading?

hypotheses.paper: a BTZ line Δ admitting a spear neighbourhood (of some vertex q), p ∈ Δ ∩ I⁻(Σ)
hypotheses.note: IsSpearNbhd q R U and p ∈ connectedComponentIn (S0 M) q. 'q in the past of p': IsFullFutureBTZRay.exists_eq_of_line + IsSpearNbhd.of_ray. 'q in the future of p' (DEC-108): exists_spearNbhd_below, the infimum of the parameters of the line in [s,0] that are spear vertices, each step CylChartData.exists_spear_below (a chart cylinder at the infimum glued to a spear chart of vertex a nearby line point above).

ContinuousOn τ_Σ (closedBall 0 R′) PROVED (continuousOn_tauS: for a < τ_Σ(z), ψ(a,z) ∉ the closed J⁺(Σ), so a < τ_Σ near z; symmetrically with J⁻(Σ)); smoothness not claimed — it needs Σ smooth spacelike (B21's transversality argument), Σ is a topological Cauchy surface here. 'positive' read as τ_Σ > v + R′/2 (B21's normalisation Φ(p) = (−R/2,0,0)). Round 0's 'only a function' justification was wrong and is withdrawn (audit major).

the open region τ > v + R′/2 above the rim of the head; Def 2.1's shaft is the boundary half-tube {r = R, τ ≥ …}. B21 Prop 2.17 (PDF l.1983) uses the conclusion as 'a circle in the shaft' (the restriction of τ_Σ to the boundary circle r = R′), consistent with this reading.

findings: B21 Lemma 2.4's proof, l.725: 'if q is in the future of q' should read 'of p'.

B21 Lemma 2.4's proof (l.746–757): the existence of the graph over D_R comes from transversality of the SMOOTH spacelike Σ at w = Σ ∩ Δ followed by shrinking R; the broken curves c_{θ0,r0} give 'at most once'. The paper's argument is complete in its smooth setting. For a topological Cauchy surface (this file) transversality is unavailable and existence over the whole disc is obtained instead from inextensibility of the vertical null rays of the spear chart (spear_vertical_noLimit, via axis_noLimit and B21 prop:isom_strong) and connectedness (spear_vertical_meets). (Round 0's finding said the paper's argument was incomplete; that was a misreading and is withdrawn.)

B21 Lemma 2.4's 'smooth positive function': in the topological setting the function is continuous (continuousOn_tauS); smoothness needs Σ smooth spacelike. 'positive' refers to the normalisation Φ(p) = (−R/2,0,0).

DEC-108, B21 Lemma 2.4's case 'q in the future of p' (l.725–733): TRUE and proved. B21 'chooses the φ_i and φ so that the changes of charts are the identity' and glues; two steps are left implicit and are where the work is: (i) a change of chart is a restriction of an isometry of 𝔼₀ only on a CONNECTED overlap (on another component of the overlap a different isometry may act), so the normalisation is made on the component U0 of the vertex (btzE0_localUnique_core + rigidity e0_eqOn_of_eqOn_open); (ii) the glued Φ must be injective, which B21 does not argue: here Φ = ψ on W1 ∪ U0 (W1 the spear above the level w+η/3) and κ⁻¹ ∘ e on U0 ∪ L (L below that level), and a point of the spear sent by ψ into the chart cylinder lies in U0 because the whole causal diamond from the vertex is sent into the (causally convex) cylinder. The finite cover of [p,q] is replaced by a continuation (infimum of the good parameters), one chart cylinder at a time.
questions: Lemma 2.4's 'in the shaft' is read as the open region τ > v + R′/2 above the head's rim (Def 2.1's shaft is the boundary half-tube); B21 Prop 2.17 (PDF l.1983) uses it as 'a circle in the shaft'. Accept this reading?

labels.label: full future BTZ rays (RamcovGX.tex:2352, step of prop:globally_hyperbolic_cauchy_complete_manifolds)

hypotheses.note: GH + Cauchy-maximal (IsE0CauchyMaximal), the corrected proposition of DEC-77(c) (counterexample {τ<0}); Cauchy-completeness unused; CBG inputs discharged in exists_fullFutureBTZRay_e0.

IsFullFutureBTZRay: γ(t) = ψ(v+t, 0) for an injective E0-morphism ψ on an open neighbourhood of the whole model ray; proved: in sing₀, injective, continuous, future directed, without future endpoint, covering the future half of its BTZ line.

findings: RamcovGX.tex:2352 cites 'Lemma 2.4 of brunswic2021cauchy' for the full future BTZ rays; the result is B21 Lemma 2.3 (lem:tube, l.635); Lemma 2.4 presupposes a spear neighbourhood. Cauchy-maximality is needed (B21 l.630: the past half {τ<0} of E0 has no spear neighbourhood), which the printed proposition does not assume (D-11, DEC-77(c)).

kb_proposals: Gluing two charted pieces with Causal.CBG.FamilyGlueData over Bool: define the piece family by `def P : Bool → Type | false => ↥A | true => ↥B` with pattern-matched instances (TopologicalSpace/ChartedSpace/HasGroupoid/T2/SC); U and φ by match on (i,j); the 8-case cocycle closes by rfl / Subtype.ext (left_inv, right_inv). Transitions as total maps via `dite` with a junk point, LiftPropOn through mathlib's ChartedSpace.liftPropWithinAt_subtypeVal_comp_iff (corestriction) and Causal.CBG.liftPropOn_{comp,mono_of_le,congr_of_eqOn,id} — no Geometry parameters needed (GX.E0Spear.CylChartData.liftPropOn_glueφ').

Hausdorffness of a chart-gluing: T2 via FamilyGlueData.t2Space_iff_isClosed_graph; the (i,i) graphs are diagonals (familyGlue_graph_self), the (j,i) graph is the swap-preimage of the (i,j) one (familyGlue_graph_swap); close the one remaining graph by keeping the overlap inside a COMPACT subset of the chart domain (GX.E0Spear.CylChartData.isClosed_graph10).

The causality of an open subset of an E0-manifold is the restricted one through Causal.CBG.Geometry.causality_restrict on e0Geometry (CE ↥W = ((CE M).restrict W).toSubtype holds by that lemma's statement up to defeq); a past open set is GloballyHyperbolicOn via GloballyHyperbolicOn.of_causallyConvexIn.
Level sets T = a of a Cauchy time function strictly increasing along ≤ are Cauchy surfaces with only IsCausal (not strong causality): GX.E0Spear.isCauchySurface_level (Inextensible.reparam + IVT).

Reading relations of a charted 𝔼₀-manifold back into the model: Causal.CBG.chartedCausality_chartIso (with E0.chartIso_mem_e0Groupoid, E0.absolutelyMinimalOn_YBTZ) composed with chartIso_paperInY gives `(CE M).le (κ⁻¹A) ↔ causality.le A` for A open in the chart target (GX.E0Spear.chart_le_iff); with a causally convex chart set (strong causality of a GH manifold, GloballyHyperbolic.stronglyCausal + E0LM.e0_tarentin) and Causality.le_of_causallyConvexIn, relations of M between chart points are model relations (GX.E0Spear.CylChartData.le_model).

When a paper says 'take the chart neighbourhood small enough so that … is acausal', put it in the data structure as a FIELD and prove it in the existence lemma; a structure that only fixes the chart target lets sorried leaves be asserted for configurations where they are false (WP-41i audit round 2).

Relative curve extension with constant pieces (WP-43a): to show a causal curve c of an open W is extensible because it lies on a T-parametrised curve γ of W reaching further in time, extend by γ ∘ h with h continuous NON-DECREASING (GX.E0Spear.causalCurveIn_comp_monotoneOn: ≤_N reflexive handles the constant pieces), after an arctan reparametrisation (Extensible.of_comp) to make the open end bounded; a greatest parameter is extensible_of_isGreatest. Consequence: GX.E0Spear.isCauchySurfaceOn_of_isPast (a Cauchy surface inside an open past set is Cauchy there).

Connectedness of a NON-compact Cauchy surface without a splitting (WP-43a): WP-41k's minimal-point argument works with R1 (J⁺(S) ∩ J⁻(q) compact, E0LM.sfa_isCompact_Jplus_inter_Jminus) in place of compactness of S; the futures of closed pieces of S are closed by a tarentin-diamond localisation (GX.E0Spear.isClosed_Jplus_of_subset_cauchy).
Causal.CBG.TwoPiece (Ppcm.lean) is the framework for causality/GH of a two-piece gluing; its mixed-diamond lemma needs a Cauchy surface common to both pieces, which a spear/tube piece never has.

An injective 𝔼₀-morphism is a Causal.Causality.PieceChart of its image without any Geometry: ← is the morphism, → its inverse on the image (Causal.CBG.liftPropOn_invFunOn + isEMorphismOn_of_isE0Mor) (GX.E0Spear.pieceChart_of_isE0Mor). With it a FamilyGlueData gluing over Bool is a TwoPiece (absolutelyMinimalOn = Causal.CBG.chartedCausality_absolutelyMinimalOn).

GH of a two-piece gluing WITHOUT a common Cauchy surface (WP-44d): causality and unmixed diamonds from TwoPiece; a mixed diamond J(x,y) is the union of two continuous images of compacts — one in the past piece M0 closed up in the ambient M (J⁺(x) ∩ J⁻(K), compact in a GH tarentin T2 spacetime by a finite cover of K by open diamonds), pushed by the map equal to ι0 on M0 and to the chart on the rest; the other in the model above the gluing level (GX.E0Spear.CylChartData.isCompact_diamond_mixed).

Transporting inextensibility to paper coordinates of 𝔼₀: CE E0Y and E0LM.D have the same ≤ on every open set (ceY_le_iff), so Causal.Causality.inextensible_congr_causality; then GX.E0CBG.isEMorphismOn_of_chartIso chartIso_paperInY with IsEMorphismOn.inextensible_iff_invComp (left inverse paperOfY) (GX.E0Spear.CylChartData.not_inextensible_above).

Gluing a chart to a spear chart along the BTZ line (WP-44d): normalise κ ∘ ψ to e = e0Lift Ψ on the connected component U0 of its domain around the vertex (the axis_noLimit template: btzE0_localUnique_core, e0_eqOn_of_eqOn_open, e0_eq_of_mem_closure); glue ψ (above a τ-level, and on U0) with κ⁻¹ ∘ e (on U0 and below the level); injectivity from the causal convexity of the chart cylinder; the new spear fits by a thickening of the axis segment (IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open). Continuation along a line: the infimum of the good parameters (GX.E0Spear.exists_spearNbhd_below).

An e0Groupoid element defined on the whole 𝔼₀ summand preserves and reflects the causal relation of 𝔼₀ (GX.E0Spear.le_iff_of_mem_e0Groupoid, chartIso_mem_e0Groupoid on range Sum.inr); on the axis this gives order-preserving maps (le_axis, le_axis_iff, le_axis_iff').
